liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help on the Way** (2 reviews): The opening Help>Slipknot>Franklin's sequence convinced the reviewer the show would be strong; The Help>Slip>Franklin's opener is very hot [7][18]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow in the first set stumbles a bit [18]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Eyes and Attics were singled out as the high points of the show [7]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The Wheel>Last Time>Attics run is the strongest part of the second set [18]
- **Attics of My Life** (1 review): Attics is probably the highlight of a rather humdrum second set [16]

## The recordings

- **gd94-03-06.sbd.kidder.8332.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 148 min; rated 3.25/5 by 24 [1]. Said about its sound: The bass drum on the left channel clips with audible pops, which spoils the recording for this reviewer; The bass drum sound is annoying and hurts ballads such as Stella; the reviewer blames Mickey for this tour's sound; Recording sounds good, maybe slightly flat, but worthwhile [8][11][12][16]
- **gd1994-03-06.sbd.sailorsaint.33613.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1994-03-06.152013.sbd.latvala.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 145 min [3]
- **gd1994-03-06.AKG451.Darby.119560.Flac1648-2448**: audience recording; 19 songs; 145 min [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer once asked Vince, whose family lives in Phoenix, about the Phoenix Stella, and he responded enthusiastically [11]
- Show started at 5:00 pm on a cool, sunny day, mellow after the previous night's fence-climbing gate crashers [12]
- Reviewer says Desert Sky still stands, now called Cricket Pavilion [12]
- Reviewer attended the run and mentions complaints about missed notes and that these were Dan Healy's last shows [13]
- Reviewer drove down from Colorado with a friend, and says the trip cost a job and a girlfriend [17]
- This was Dan Healy's last show as the band's sound engineer; he was fired afterward [3]
- Jim Blackwood and John Bradford interviewed Healy on March 5 before the show; the interview circulates transcribed [3]
- Reviewer found it not a super spectacular show [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-03-06.sbd.kidder.8332.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD --> DAT --> CDR [1]. Also: Soundboard to DAT to CDR, via Charlie Kidder [1]
- **gd1994-03-06.sbd.sailorsaint.33613.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Sailor_Saint; source: SBD > ? > CDR [2]. Also: Cloned by Dick Latvala in summer 1999 from the March 4-6 1994 run for a Grateful Dead radio show host; Uploader boosted levels about 18%, adjusted some track markers and fixed a duplicated section between Drums and Space [2]
- **gd1994-03-06.152013.sbd.latvala.flac16**: transferred by Fresh transfer and mastering by Jim Blackwood Sony R-500 to Tascam DA-3000 [2020] Track FLAC and Pack by Mark Goldey; source: SBD > DAT 44.1 kHz [3]. Also: Minor patches in Let It Grow and Attics of My Life come from a Schoeps MK4 audience recording [3]
- **gd1994-03-06.AKG451.Darby.119560.Flac1648-2448**: taped by Mike Darby; transferred by Keo; source: flac16/48kHz & flac24 ; Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; AKG451EB/CK1's (DIN/DFC/First 1/4 Of OTS/9 Feet High)> Whirlwind Phantoms>Teac DA-P20 @ 16/48… [4]

## Art and photos
